purpose: Treat witness position as an evidentiary and ethical axis: who speaks, what they can see, what they cannot know, and what authority the archive must not give them.
principles: Every death record should state whose perspective it carries and whose perspective it lacks.
A role can be close to the body and still wrong about meaning; a role can be official and still miss the room; a role can be nonprofessional and still see what matters.
First-person testimony has special authority over experience and wishes, but still needs consent, context, communication support, and delirium/sedation boundaries.
Worker knowledge is part of the corpus; worker exposure, employment risk, and compassion fatigue must be protected.
No role label should be used to settle family conflicts, legal authority, clinical truth, or spiritual meaning.

clusters.name: the person dying or surviving a near-death state
what_the_role_can_add: communication by word, gesture, device, or silence
clusters.danger: proxying interiority or making survivor reports a universal afterlife map

clusters.name: family, intimate, and relational witnesses
clusters.danger: letting legal next-of-kin status erase chosen family or letting family memory become clinical fact

clusters.name: hospice and palliative team witnesses
clusters.danger: credential hierarchy, scope creep, and assuming professional language is the whole death

clusters.name: institutional, emergency, and official witnesses
clusters.danger: official narrative, emergency protocol, or role authority replacing lived testimony

clusters.name: deathcare, disposition, and after-the-death witnesses
clusters.danger: technical spectacle, funeral advice, or treating grief professionals as diagnosticians

clusters.name: vulnerable, involuntary, and absent witnesses
clusters.danger: extracting from children, bystanders, workers, or absence itself

review_rule: Public rendering must name the witness position, missing positions, and authority boundary before interpreting any record.
